approachQuestion.prompt:
A batch contains exactly two distinct values that occur once each; every other value occurs exactly twice. Return the two once-occurring values in either order.

Constraints: 2 <= n <= 200000; n is even; values are unsigned 32-bit words.
Example: [14,5,9,14,2,9] -> [5,2]. Edge case: [0,4294967295] -> [0,4294967295].

Choose the best approach under these constraints.
constraints: Unsigned 32-bit XOR, AND and modular negation cost constant time; output consists of two words.
Inputs are read-only. Include all temporary storage and any call stack; exclude the supplied input and the returned output. No input copy is implicit.

options.text: XOR all values to get d. Isolate any set bit of d, then XOR values separately according to that bit. Return the two group results.
options.feedback: The two singles differ at that bit, so they separate; each duplicate pair stays together and cancels.

options.text: Count values in a hash map, then return the two keys with count one.
options.feedback: Counts solve the full domain, but use a growing table. Lookup/update is expected constant time under uniform hashing.

options.text: Always partition by bit zero and XOR each group.
options.feedback: For [2,4], both singles have bit zero clear. This returns 6 and 0 instead of 2 and 4.

options.text: Return the XOR of all values together with zero.
options.feedback: For [2,4], the XOR 6 is neither single; the second value is not necessarily zero.

feedback.reason: The XOR of the two singles has a set bit where they differ.
details: First compute the XOR of the entire batch. Its nonzero bits identify positions where the two singles differ. Choose one such bit, rescan the batch, and cancel pairs within each of the two groups.

The XOR of the two singles has a set bit where they differ. Partition by that bit; duplicate pairs stay together and cancel inside a group. Summing or sorting values is unnecessary under this multiplicity promise.

“XOR all values to get d. Isolate any set bit of d, then XOR values separately according to that bit. Return the two group results.”: The two singles differ at that bit, so they separate; each duplicate pair stays together and cancels.
“Count values in a hash map, then return the two keys with count one.”: Counts solve the full domain, but use a growing table. Lookup/update is expected constant time under uniform hashing.
“Always partition by bit zero and XOR each group.”: For [2,4], both singles have bit zero clear. This returns 6 and 0 instead of 2 and 4.
“Return the XOR of all values together with zero.”: For [2,4], the XOR 6 is neither single; the second value is not necessarily zero.

complexityQuestion.prompt: For split-on-differing-bit, choose the tightest worst-case time and auxiliary-space pair. Let n be the batch length.
constraints: Unsigned 32-bit XOR, AND and modular negation cost constant time; output consists of two words.
Inputs are read-only. Include all temporary storage and any call stack; exclude the supplied input and the returned output. No input copy is implicit.

feedback.reason: Two full scans keep only a few word accumulators.
details: Two full scans use a fixed number of word accumulators. No table, copy or recursion is needed.
Unsigned 32-bit XOR, AND and modular negation cost constant time; output consists of two words.
“O(n) time, O(n) auxiliary space”: The analyzed method does not retain a table or copy.
“O(n²) time, O(1) auxiliary space”: This is looser than the bounded number of scans.
“O(1) time, O(1) auxiliary space”: The input cannot be processed without scanning it in the worst case.
